channel.title: Crypto Node Dispatch
channel.description: Daily crypto reporting on network performance, validator economics, protocol changes and market structure, grounded in on-chain data and primary sources.

item.title: Crypto Tax Lots Enter Broker Reporting, but DeFi Stays Manual
item.description: Broker basis reporting now covers some 2026 crypto purchases, but self-custody, transfers and DeFi still require wallet-level records and timely lot choices.

item.title: Universal Bridge Keeps uAsset Minting Behind Merchant Gate
item.description: Permissioned Merchants execute uAsset mints, while verified users can request issuance—a model that saves liquidity but concentrates operational trust.

item.title: Airdrop Eligibility Turns Wallet History Into a Score
item.description: Airdrop eligibility converts activity into points, applies snapshot cutoffs and Sybil filters, then assigns tokens without proving who controls each address.

item.title: Bitcoin Difficulty's 1.31% Rise Shows the Retarget at Work
item.description: Bitcoin's retarget turns block timing into a cost reset every 2,016 blocks, stabilizing issuance while forcing miners to absorb each new benchmark.

item.title: Manta Bridge Deposits Created Yield-Bearing Claims
item.description: Manta’s New Paradigm replaced bridged ETH and USDC with yield-bearing STONE and wUSDM, adding utility but also new accounting and redemption risks.

item.title: Tokenization Gives Physical Assets New Rails, Not New Liquidity
item.description: Tokenized property gains divisible ownership and faster transfers, but operators inherit registry, custody and liquidity work that blockchains cannot settle.

item.title: Five Reasons SyncSwap Classic Pools Begin at 50/50
item.description: SyncSwap's 50/50 Classic Pool design sets a neutral launch price, keeps liquidity two-sided and simple, but leaves LPs carrying rebalancing risk.

item.title: UNI Vote Puts Governance Inside Uniswap v4 Fee Logic
item.description: UNI’s July vote shows governance tokens can turn policy into executable fee rules, but operators inherit new margin, monitoring and control costs.

item.title: Why Orphaned Blocks Fall Out of Bitcoin's Canonical History
item.description: Bitcoin drops valid competing blocks when another branch gains more work, costing miners rewards while preserving one canonical transaction history for nodes.

item.title: Pectra Raised the Stakes for Hardware Wallet Screens
item.description: Pectra made wallet signatures more powerful, turning the hardware screen from a key-storage accessory into the last trusted check on transaction intent.

item.title: LSE, Payward Plan 100 UK Stock Tokens and Native Shares
item.description: LSE and Payward will bring 100 London-listed equities to xStocks, testing whether regulated settlement can make token wrappers durable infrastructure.

item.title: Meta Earth Vote Clears V2.0.17 for Block 14,920,300
item.description: Meta Earth validators unanimously approved V2.0.17, committing operators to a coordinated restart at block 14,920,300 and an estimated eight-hour outage.

item.title: Velora Brings Cross-Chain Orders to Robinhood Chain
item.description: Velora adds intent-based swaps and automated orders to Robinhood Chain, but traders still need fill data to prove lower costs after gas and bridge fees.

item.title: Core Lightning 26.06.7: Check the Artifact Before Restart
item.description: Core Lightning 26.06.7 fixes undisclosed flaws; Docker users must verify image digests, while VLS operators must update a version gate before restart.

item.title: Canonical Means Who Controls the Claim
item.description: Canonical identifies the token recognized as authoritative on a chain, while other bridged versions remain claims that depend on a bridge’s custody and code.

item.title: Lock-and-Mint Tokens Are Claims, Not New Value
item.description: Lock-and-mint systems expand token access by issuing a claim against locked assets, but custody, redemption delays, and governance decide who absorbs the loss.
